objective: A frozen exploratory measure on the same families: at each full level, how many paths keep all three contacts persistent and how many of those are native, with the last contact's row period; and a map of shapes around 3/5/5/3 (end rings of 3 to 5 cells, middle rings of 4 to 7 with antipodal contacts, every linear rule and law) counting persistent and native paths per shape. Does growth break persistence or composition, and is 3/5/5/3 isolated?
status: Supported 2026-11-08 (exploratory): growth breaks composition, not persistence. At every full level persistent paths remain (424 to 12,916, mostly with row periods of at most 12) and none is native. In the map of 90 shapes around 3/5/5/3 (368,640,000 paths), native paths occur at 3 of the 36 size combinations: 3/5/5/3 (16), 5/6/6/5 (48, rule 90 end rings and 60/102 middles) and 4/7/7/5 (16), each family at one shape only; control reproduced PATH-HYBRID-20261108-001A's counts.
title: Where growth breaks a native path
